subject: OrbitAI renewal: proposal for reserved GPU expansion & overflow policy
body_preview: Proposed committed pool increase + soft overflow credits; suggested 12-month term with throughput SLO and on-demand spillover pricing tier.
messages:
From: David Liu <dave@orbitai.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 02 Aug 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase questions

Hi Chloe,

We're approaching our renewal window and want to discuss increasing our reserved GPU pool. Q2 usage spiked due to new features and we need guaranteed throughput for inference during peak times. Two key asks: 1) add ~40% more reserved GPUs (Nvidia A800 equivalent), and 2) a predictable overflow policy — we prefer on-demand spillover with clear per-token/cost caps rather than a hard reject.

Can you share a proposal with pricing, expected latency SLOs, and what the overflow behavior would look like if on-demand capacity is exhausted? Also loop in procurement when you have the numbers.

Thanks,
Dave
Director of Engineering, OrbitAI

---
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: David Liu <dave@orbitai.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Aug 2025 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase questions

Hi Dave — thanks for the context and the heads-up on Q2. Attached is a first-pass proposal (OrbitAI_Renewal_Expansion_Proposal_v2.pdf) and a short workbook showing throughput vs cost assumptions (SLA_Throughput_Metrics_Q2.xlsx). High-level summary below and next steps.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Committed capacity: increase reserved pool by 45% (from 200 -> 290 A800-equivalent GPUs) on a 12-month renewal.
- Throughput guarantees: we provide a 99th-percentile latency SLO of 190ms for 1.5k token requests at the committed throughput (measured per route).
- Overflow policy: primary approach is on-demand spillover (preferred) with two safeguards:
  1) Soft overflow credits: OrbitAI receives a monthly buffer of on-demand credits (equivalent to ~10% of committed throughput) billed at the on-demand rate but capped to protect against runaway spend.
  2) Hard cap fallback: if the combination of committed + soft credits + on-demand pool exceeds region capacity, we will notify and then apply a controlled throttle to low-priority routes after attempting routing to alternate regions (per your policy).
- Pricing: blended committed rate for the 45% increase with tiered on-demand pricing tiers. See attached PDF for line items.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus and I finalize the formal SOW and SLA wording (I'll draft today).
2) If acceptable, procurement can start the PO; we'll send a DocuSign link for the addendum.
3) Ops will schedule a technical ramp (2-week provisioning window to add reserved GPUs).

cc: Marcus — can you confirm the latency SLO and whether the soft credit sizing looks conservative enough from an ops perspective?

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: OrbitAI_Renewal_Expansion_Proposal_v2.pdf (proposal, 6 pages)
Attachment: SLA_Throughput_Metrics_Q2.xlsx (workbook)

---
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Aug 2025 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: OrbitAI — overflow mechanics and ops constraints

Chloe / Laura — quick internal on the proposal Chloe sent to Orbit. I reviewed the ops feasibility with infra: increasing the committed pool by 45% in-region is achievable but will require one of two paths: (A) reassign available hosts in us-west-2 and do a rolling re-provision; ETA ~10 business days from signed PO, or (B) deploy burst capacity in us-west-1 as overflow — faster (~3-5 days) but adds cross-region egress considerations.

On the overflow design: the soft credit buffer is good; ops suggests we add a fail-safe in the SOW that includes: 1) a per-minute spike guard (if sustained >150% committed for >15 minutes trigger automatic auto-scale request to cloud partner), 2) explicit per-route priority to allow graceful throttling of non-critical routes, and 3) a monthly reconciliation report showing overflow usage and credit burn.

For pricing, Finance wants to avoid open-ended on-demand liability — suggest we cap monthly on-demand spend at 200% of the committed monthly bill unless Orbit signs a higher spend cap. We'll present a tiered surcharge that kicks in past that.

I'll draft the SOW language for the fail-safes and the billing cap. Chloe — if you want I can join the call with Procurement.

-marcus
VP, Customer Success (internal note)

---
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: David Liu <dave@orbitai.com>, Procurement <procurement@orbitai.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Revised proposal and SOW language for overflow protection

Hi Dave / Procurement team — per our internal review we've updated the proposal to include the operational fail-safes Marcus recommended and a billing cap structure. Key changes in v2:
- Added per-minute spike guard threshold and auto-scale escalation steps.
- Per-route priority flags to allow you to mark low-latency critical routes vs batch jobs.
- Billing cap: default monthly on-demand spend cap at 200% of committed monthly spend; option to opt into higher cap with a reduced surcharge.
- Monthly overflow reconciliation report delivered to OrbitAI stakeholders.

I've attached the revised PDF and the SOW excerpt is included on page 4. If these terms look good, we'll issue a DocuSign addendum for signature and start the provisioning timeline once the PO is received.

Permissions / procurement note: procurement@orbitai.com — please reply with your PO template or confirm if you need a line-item quote. We can provide a separate billing addendum for your AP team.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the SOW language.

Best,
Chloe
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: OrbitAI_Renewal_Expansion_Proposal_v2.pdf (updated with SOW excerpt)

---
From: David Liu <dave@orbitai.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orbitai.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@orbitai.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2025 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Revised proposal and SOW language for overflow protection

Thanks Chloe — this looks sensible and the fail-safes address the big risks for us. Two quick asks before we sign: 1) can we get a short runbook that explains the route-priority settings and how to set them from our console (ops needs this for our runbooks), and 2) please include an example monthly reconciliation report (just a template) with the DocuSign packet.

Procurement — please advise if Orbit needs a formal quote or if the attached PDF + DocuSign addendum is sufficient. We'll aim to return a signed addendum by EOD Friday assuming no surprises.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Dave
Director of Engineering, OrbitAI
